items.title: Regular two-level fractions, signed defining relations, and resolution
items.statement: Given p linearly independent factor words G_i in F_2^k and signs s_i, the regular fraction is the set of full-factorial runs satisfying x_{G_i}=s_i. The signed defining subgroup H is generated by (s_i,G_i), with multiplication (ε,A)(δ,B)=(εδ,A△B); a word has length |A| and resolution is the shortest nonidentity length in H. The local alias theorem proves the run count, the exact subgroup, and its column interpretation.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §§18.2 and 18.4

items.title: The defining subgroup gives the exact alias relations
items.statement: For p independent generator equations, the regular fraction has 2^{k-p} runs and its signed defining subgroup H has 2^p elements. For effects A,B, their columns agree exactly when (+1,A△B)∈H and are negatives exactly when (−1,A△B)∈H; H contains all and only signed monomial relations that are constant +1 on the fraction.
items.strategy: Encode signs by bits, row-reduce the p independent equations, characterize the monomials constant on the free-coordinate solution set, and compare the A and B columns by their symmetric difference.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §18.2

items.title: Aliased factorial columns prevent separate coefficient identification
items.statement: In the unrestricted fixed-design linear model Y=Xβ+ε, with the error law independent of β, if two distinct factorial columns satisfy c_A=σc_B for σ∈{+1,−1}, their contribution depends only on σβ_A+β_B. Varying β_A and β_B while preserving that combination leaves the full response law unchanged, so the two coefficients are not separately identifiable without a restriction or additional design rows.
items.strategy: Group the two equal-or-opposite column contributions and exhibit a nonzero parameter direction that leaves the fitted vector, hence the response law, unchanged.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §18.6
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §5.3.3.4.3, Confounding (also called aliasing)

items.title: Full and partial foldovers separate aliases by parity
items.statement: For a mirror foldover reversing all factor signs, a defining word of order r changes sign by (−1)^r. For a partial foldover reversing the selected factor set J, a word (ε,A) changes sign by (−1)^{|A∩J|}. The residual defining subgroup is H_J={ (ε,A)∈H: |A∩J| is even }; thus originally signed-aliased effects remain aliased exactly for even parity, while odd-parity relations are separated.
items.strategy: Evaluate each signed monomial on the transformed runs, identify the relations that hold on both the original and appended fractions, and apply the exact alias criterion.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §18.7
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §§5.3.3.8.1–5.3.3.8.2, Mirror-Image and Alternative Foldover Designs

title: Fractional factorial aliases and foldover — Examples

items.title: The alias classes in a $2^{3-1}$ fraction
items.statement: For the regular 2^{3−1} fraction generated by I=ABC, the complete equal-column alias classes are {I,ABC}, {A,BC}, {B,AC}, and {C,AB}. In the unrestricted model each pair contributes through its coefficient sum, so sparsity or hierarchy is an additional assumption rather than a design conclusion.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §18.2

items.title: Full and targeted foldovers of a resolution III fraction
items.statement: For the 2^{5−2} fraction generated by I=ABD and I=CDE, the defining subgroup is {I,ABD,CDE,ABCE}. A full mirror foldover leaves {I,ABCE}, while reversing only factor A leaves {I,CDE}; the latter still aliases C with DE and remains resolution III. The residual alias pairs are exactly S with S△ABCE for the full foldover and S with S△CDE for the partial foldover.

references.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, Chapter 18, §§18.2, 18.4, and 18.7
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §5.3.3.8, Improving Fractional Factorial Design Resolution
